title: Uniform distribution of junta coefficient inputs
statement: Let $n,k$ be natural numbers, let $P\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $\delta$ be a rational number with $0<\delta\leq 1/2$, and choose a member $S$ of the family of subsets of the free coordinates of size at most the cutoff associated with $k$. If a batch of restricted assignments is chosen uniformly, then extracting the coefficient-input rows indexed by $S$ gives a uniformly distributed batch of sign vectors of the prescribed coefficient sample count, with one sign for each free coordinate.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite set of indices in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
$S$ belongs to the low-degree Fourier family determined by $P$ and $k$
caveat: The statement uses several sample-count and sign-cube constructions whose informal definitions were not supplied; the description identifies their roles from the formal definitions.
